title: All Accounted for After Tanker Crashes Into Docked New Orleans Riverboat
summary: Search and rescue operations were continuing after the riverboat, which had 129 people aboard, was struck by a tanker ship on Friday afternoon, the authorities said.

A tanker ship struck a riverboat carrying 129 people on Friday in New Orleans, causing the cruise ship to capsize at its dock and prompting a wide-scale search and rescue operation, the authorities said.


Mayor Helena Moreno of New Orleans said at a news conference that all passengers of the riverboat, the American Heritage, were accounted for after the crash. She added that 32 people were at local hospitals, none with critical injuries.


Capt. Melanie A. Burnham, commander of Sector New Orleans for the U.S. Coast Guard, praised the work of those who rescued the ship’s passengers.


“I want to recognize the dedication, professionalism and bravery of all those first responders,” she said.


“This is a literal miracle on the Mississippi,” said Gov. Jeff Landry of Louisiana, who also spoke at the news conference.


Image


The riverboat American Heritage was struck on Friday by another ship while docked in New Orleans, according to American Cruise Lines, which operates the boat.
